content.intro: CLI scripts and background jobs need explicit inputs, predictable exit behavior, bounded resource use, observable failures, and safe retry semantics. Long-running work should not rely on a browser request staying open. In this lesson, focus on work that should not block a web request; then compare it with message queues. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use asynchronous processing concepts when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: CLI scripts and background jobs need explicit inputs, predictable exit behavior, bounded resource use, observable failures, and safe retry semantics. Long-running work should not rely on a browser request staying open. For asynchronous processing concepts, begin with work that should not block a web request. Also distinguish message queues; event-driven architectures; concurrency and asynchronous runtime libraries. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
